title: Creational Design Patterns
description: Singleton (Meyers & Thread-safe), Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, and Prototype in modern C++.

topics.title: Singleton (Meyers Singleton & Concurrency)
topics.description: Ensuring a class has exactly one instance and providing a global point of access.

sections.title: 1. What is it?
sections.content: The Singleton Pattern guarantees that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to that instance.

sections.title: 2. Why do we need it?
sections.content: Useful for shared physical resources: Logger instance, Thread Pool coordinator, Hardware Device Controller.

sections.title: 3. Core idea
sections.content: Private constructor + Deleted copy/move operations + Static instance method (Meyers Singleton).

sections.title: 4. How it works
sections.content: In C++11 and later, static local variable initialization in a function is guaranteed by the language standard to be thread-safe without manual mutex locks (Meyers Singleton).

sections.title: 5. Visual explanation
sections.content: Visual Architecture & Mechanics:

callout.title: Meyers Singleton Thread Safety
callout.text: C++11 Standard [§6.7]: Static local variables are initialized exactly once, even when accessed simultaneously by multiple threads. Zero manual mutex locking required!

sections.title: 6. C++ implementation
sections.content: Complete Production C++20 Implementation:

sections.title: 7. Code walkthrough
sections.content: Meyers Singleton using static local variable, deleted copy/move, thread-safe access.

sections.title: 8. Real-world example
sections.content: Application Configuration Managers, Database Connection Pools, Hardware Serial Ports.

sections.title: 9. When to use
sections.content: Use when exactly one coordinating instance must exist across the entire process lifetime.

sections.title: 10. When NOT to use
sections.content: Do not use as a glorified global variable bag; harms testability.

sections.title: 11. Advantages
sections.content: Guaranteed single instance, lazy initialization, zero manual mutex overhead.

sections.title: 12. Disadvantages
sections.content: Hidden dependencies; difficult to unit test with mock replacements.

sections.title: 13. Variations / Types
sections.content: Meyers Singleton, Eager Singleton, Double-Checked Locking Pattern (legacy).

sections.title: 14. Common mistakes
sections.content: Writing complex manual Double-Checked Locking with mutexes when Meyers Singleton is 10x cleaner.

sections.title: 15. Interview questions
sections.content: Q: Why is Meyers Singleton thread-safe in C++11?

sections.title: 16. Interview answer
sections.content: Answer: The C++11 standard mandates that local static variables are initialized concurrently safe by the runtime during first function entry (magic statics).

sections.title: 17. Practice problem
sections.content: Build a thread-safe ConfigurationManager singleton.

referenceCode.code: class Config { Config() = default; public: Config(const Config&) = delete; static Config& get() { static Config inst; return inst; } };

sections.title: 18. Summary
sections.content: Mastering Singleton (Meyers Singleton & Concurrency) is essential for advanced Low-Level Design interviews.

topics.title: Factory Method Pattern
topics.description: Defining an interface for creating an object, but letting subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

sections.title: 1. What is it?
sections.content: Factory Method defines an interface for creating objects, but lets derived subclasses or static factory routines decide which concrete class to instantiate.

sections.title: 2. Why do we need it?
sections.content: Decouples client creation code from concrete derived class constructors.

sections.title: 3. Core idea
sections.content: Call a creation method instead of calling new ConcreteClass() directly.

sections.title: 4. How it works
sections.content: Client calls VehicleFactory::createVehicle(type) returning a std::unique_ptr<IVehicle>.

sections.title: 5. Visual explanation
sections.content: Visual Architecture & Mechanics:

callout.title: Factory Method Flow
callout.text: Client -> Factory::create(type) -> returns std::unique_ptr<IVehicle> -> Client uses interface

sections.title: 6. C++ implementation
sections.content: Complete Production C++20 Implementation:

sections.title: 7. Code walkthrough
sections.content: VehicleFactory centralizes construction and returns unique_ptr interface.

sections.title: 8. Real-world example
sections.content: Document parsing (PDF vs Word vs JSON), payment gateway selection.

sections.title: 9. When to use
sections.content: Use when creation logic involves complex decisions or varies based on parameters.

sections.title: 10. When NOT to use
sections.content: Do not use for trivial classes that only have a single constructor.

sections.title: 11. Advantages
sections.content: Adheres to Single Responsibility & Open/Closed principles.

sections.title: 12. Disadvantages
sections.content: Requires creating factory abstractions.

sections.title: 13. Variations / Types
sections.content: Static Factory Method, Polymorphic Factory Method (Virtual Creator).

sections.title: 14. Common mistakes
sections.content: Returning raw pointers instead of std::unique_ptr.

sections.title: 15. Interview questions
sections.content: Q: Why should Factory Methods return std::unique_ptr in modern C++?

sections.title: 16. Interview answer
sections.content: Answer: Because std::unique_ptr explicitly expresses exclusive ownership transfer from the factory to the caller with zero memory leak risk.

sections.title: 17. Practice problem
sections.content: Build a DocumentParser factory for JSON and XML.

practice.title: Document Parser Factory
practice.problemStatement: Build a DocumentParser factory for JSON and XML.

referenceCode.code: class Parser { public: virtual ~Parser() = default; }; class Factory { public: static std::unique_ptr<Parser> create(int); };

sections.title: 18. Summary
sections.content: Mastering Factory Method Pattern is essential for advanced Low-Level Design interviews.

topics.title: Abstract Factory Pattern
topics.description: Creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.

sections.title: 1. What is it?
sections.content: Abstract Factory provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects (e.g. Mac vs Windows UI buttons and scrollbars).

sections.title: 2. Why do we need it?
sections.content: Ensures that products from the same family are always used together without mixing incompatible UI components.

sections.title: 3. Core idea
sections.content: A factory of factories: IGUIFactory creates both IButton and IScrollBar.

sections.title: 4. How it works
sections.content: Client receives an IGUIFactory (e.g. MacFactory) and creates all UI components from it consistently.

sections.title: 5. Visual explanation
sections.content: Visual Architecture & Mechanics:

sections.title: 6. C++ implementation
sections.content: Complete Production C++20 Implementation:

sections.title: 7. Code walkthrough
sections.content: MacFactory and WindowsFactory create matching UI component suites.

sections.title: 8. Real-world example
sections.content: Cross-platform OS rendering engines (Qt, Flutter), Database driver suites (Postgres vs Oracle connection+command+transaction).

sections.title: 9. When to use
sections.content: Use when an application needs to configure full product families consistently.

sections.title: 10. When NOT to use
sections.content: Do not use when you only need to instantiate single unrelated objects (use Factory Method).

sections.title: 11. Advantages
sections.content: Guarantees product compatibility across a family.

sections.title: 12. Disadvantages
sections.content: Adding a new product type requires modifying the abstract factory interface.

sections.title: 13. Variations / Types
sections.content: Cross-platform Theme Factories, Database Driver Suites.

sections.title: 14. Common mistakes
sections.content: Mixing components from different concrete factories.

sections.title: 15. Interview questions
sections.content: Q: What is the difference between Factory Method and Abstract Factory?

sections.title: 16. Interview answer
sections.content: Answer: Factory Method creates ONE product using inheritance/delegation. Abstract Factory creates FAMILIES of related products using object composition.

sections.title: 17. Practice problem
sections.content: Implement a Theme factory producing Panels and Buttons.

practice.title: Dark/Light Theme Factory
practice.problemStatement: Implement a Theme factory producing Panels and Buttons.

referenceCode.code: class ITheme { public: virtual ~ITheme() = default; virtual std::unique_ptr<IButton> btn() = 0; };

sections.title: 18. Summary
sections.content: Mastering Abstract Factory Pattern is essential for advanced Low-Level Design interviews.

topics.title: Builder Pattern & Fluent Interfaces
topics.description: Separating the construction of a complex object from its representation.

sections.title: 1. What is it?
sections.content: Builder Pattern constructs complex objects step-by-step, allowing the same construction process to create different representations.

sections.title: 2. Why do we need it?
sections.content: Constructors with 10+ parameters (Telescoping Constructor anti-pattern) are error-prone.

sections.title: 3. Core idea
sections.content: Step-by-step configuration via fluent method chaining returning *this or dedicated Director.

sections.title: 4. How it works
sections.content: HttpRequest::Builder().setUrl("...").setMethod("POST").build().

sections.title: 5. Visual explanation
sections.content: Visual Architecture & Mechanics:

callout.title: Telescoping Constructor Solution
callout.text: Before: Pizza(size, cheese, pepperoni, bacon, olives, onions, mushrooms...) -> Horrible!\nAfter: Pizza::Builder().setSize(12).addCheese().addPepperoni().build();

sections.title: 6. C++ implementation
sections.content: Complete Production C++20 Implementation:

sections.title: 7. Code walkthrough
sections.content: Nested Builder class constructing UserProfile step-by-step with clean fluent syntax.

sections.title: 8. Real-world example
sections.content: SQL Query Builders, HTTP Request Builders, Game Character Customizers.

sections.title: 9. When to use
sections.content: Use when constructing objects with multiple optional configuration parameters.

sections.title: 10. When NOT to use
sections.content: Do not use for simple objects with 1-3 mandatory fields.

sections.title: 11. Advantages
sections.content: Readable, self-documenting code; avoids telescoping constructors.

sections.title: 12. Disadvantages
sections.content: Requires creating a separate Builder class.

sections.title: 13. Variations / Types
sections.content: Fluent Builder, Director-driven Builder, Inner Static Builder.

sections.title: 14. Common mistakes
sections.content: Forgetting to validate required fields inside build().

sections.title: 15. Interview questions
sections.content: Q: What problem does the Builder pattern solve?

sections.title: 16. Interview answer
sections.content: Answer: It eliminates Telescoping Constructors (constructors with dozens of confusing parameters) and supports step-by-step immutable object creation.

sections.title: 17. Practice problem
sections.content: Build a Computer configuration builder (CPU, RAM, GPU, Storage).

practice.title: Computer Hardware Builder
practice.problemStatement: Build a Computer configuration builder (CPU, RAM, GPU, Storage).

referenceCode.code: class Computer { public: class Builder { /* fluent methods */ }; };

sections.title: 18. Summary
sections.content: Mastering Builder Pattern & Fluent Interfaces is essential for advanced Low-Level Design interviews.

topics.title: Prototype Pattern & Virtual Clone Idiom
topics.description: Creating new objects by copying an existing instance using virtual clone methods.

sections.title: 1. What is it?
sections.content: Prototype Pattern creates new objects by duplicating existing instances (cloning) rather than going through fresh constructor initialization.

sections.title: 2. Why do we need it?
sections.content: When creating an object from scratch is computationally expensive (e.g. Loading 3D mesh files or database lookups).

sections.title: 3. Core idea
sections.content: Virtual copy constructor: virtual std::unique_ptr<IShape> clone() const = 0;.

sections.title: 4. How it works
sections.content: Subclasses implement clone() by calling their copy constructor and returning a new std::unique_ptr.

sections.title: 5. Visual explanation
sections.content: Visual Architecture & Mechanics:

callout.title: Virtual Copy Idiom
callout.text: C++ has no virtual copy constructor by default. The Prototype Pattern solves this by adding virtual clone() const = 0!

sections.title: 6. C++ implementation
sections.content: Complete Production C++20 Implementation:

sections.title: 7. Code walkthrough
sections.content: Virtual clone method returning unique_ptr copy of Monster instance.

sections.title: 8. Real-world example
sections.content: Game NPC spawning, Graphic shape stamping tools, Network packet template duplicating.

sections.title: 9. When to use
sections.content: Use when object creation cost is high or when cloning objects of unknown runtime types.

sections.title: 10. When NOT to use
sections.content: Do not use when objects hold non-copyable unique handles.

sections.title: 11. Advantages
sections.content: Fast $O(1)$ object spawning; polymorphic copy capability.

sections.title: 12. Disadvantages
sections.content: Deep copying complex circular reference graphs can be challenging.

sections.title: 13. Variations / Types
sections.content: Shallow Prototype, Deep Prototype with custom copy-and-swap.

sections.title: 14. Common mistakes
sections.content: Performing shallow copies on internal heap pointers.

sections.title: 15. Interview questions
sections.content: Q: How do you implement a Virtual Copy Constructor in C++?

sections.title: 16. Interview answer
sections.content: Answer: By declaring a pure virtual clone method (e.g. virtual unique_ptr clone() const = 0;) and implementing it in derived classes using return make_unique(*this);.

sections.title: 17. Practice problem
sections.content: Implement Bullet prototype with clone() for high-speed particle spawning.

practice.title: Game Bullet Prototype
practice.problemStatement: Implement Bullet prototype with clone() for high-speed particle spawning.

referenceCode.code: class Bullet { public: virtual std::unique_ptr<Bullet> clone() const { return std::make_unique<Bullet>(*this); } };

sections.title: 18. Summary
sections.content: Mastering Prototype Pattern & Virtual Clone Idiom is essential for advanced Low-Level Design interviews.
